shared-needs.rule: shared/ belongs to the shared author (brief C, "What R-03 produces"); this volume never writes it and never points into it before it exists. Each need names the volume and the anchor the shared author declares. check.sh (N-46) resolves a need by volume and anchor once the shared volume lands, so a need becomes a live pointer without a hand edit. The same needs are returned to the shared author as data by the seat that wrote this volume.
shared-needs.need: Rows for backup.started 100; backup 201; backup.busy 423; backup.failed 500; backup.mirror_failed 500; backup.rotten 500; backup.disk 503. Owner-acts: backup.failed; backup.rotten; backup.disk after N-45 ran; backup.mirror_failed when it persists a day.

backups(id, at, class, path, bytes, checksum, inner_checksum, epoch, high_water_seq, row_count, min_retained_seq, verified, mirror_path, mirror_checksum, pruned_at); entities backup:latest (compare-and-swap) and backup:running (expected absent); written only by the statement backups.append.
Backups, logs and state live under the state root with a README and a cleanup script each (C35); the hand backup tree is disposed of by N-49.
No node selects the owner's privileged AWS profile; a cloud mirror is the owner's own user-initiated script (global hard rule).

backup.interval_seconds, backup.min_interval_seconds, backup.snapshot_seconds, backup.verify_seconds, backup.mirror_seconds, backup.min_free_mib, backup.retention, backup.rpo_offhost_hours, backup.mirror_dir; the defaults are the shared config-key rows, cited, never restated.

The service restarts mid-run: temps under tmp/ removed at start, the maintenance lease backup:store expires or is swept by N-02 recover, a due backup runs at once; nothing is lost because the live store is never the thing being written.
Free space under backup.min_free_mib (default 2048 MiB, the one floor): backup.disk 503 once, run skipped, N-45 cleanup, then one card if still under.

purpose.is: N-05 is the answer to the catch the owner asked about on C34 ("whats the catch here?"): one store on one host is one box, so the store is copied on a schedule, verified, classed for retention, mirrored off the host, and every copy is a record; how old the newest off-host copy is, is a gauge with an alarm (backup.rpo_offhost_hours).
It is the only path by which N-01's restore runbook gets a file to restore from, and it is what cleanup-store.sh checks before it may delete the live file.
purpose.is-not: It does not prune (N-45 does, from the retention class on each backup record), does not back up the repository (git is its own backup), and never uses the owner's privileged AWS profile or any credential the owner did not place in the unit's environment.
purpose.decisions: D10 (C34: one store, backups scheduled per the catch), D04 (C35: artifacts in the state root with cleanup scripts), D22 (the host's crash history: eleven bugchecks in seven weeks, L10 section 5.3).

record.field: tick (every backup.interval_seconds 21600), daily (the first tick after 03:00Z), monthly (the first daily of a UTC month). The class is decided by N-06's schedule, not here, so the retention class is data on the tick.

also.from: N-50 before cut-over records, N-49 before each unlanded cleanup step (04-UNLANDED section 12 step 1), the restore runbook, and the ctl CLI
also.note: an extra backup of class manual; bounded by backup.min_interval_seconds 60
the source: a copy made on N-01's reader connection with its epoch, high_water_seq, row_count and min_retained_seq; the backup never opens coq.db and never holds the writer

record.field: N-45 reads this record by $ref to record.schema.json#/$defs/backup (NF-D1); the shape is defined here once.
sha256 of the compressed file; a second sha256 of the uncompressed database file inside.

From the Snapshot reply: the store epoch, the highest seq in the copy, the number of records in it and the retention floor at copy time. seq is strictly increasing but not gapless, so the counts are compared with row_count, never with the seq (shared/contracts.xml#epoch-cursor). A restore knows exactly which records it loses: those of the epoch after high_water_seq.
tick, daily, monthly, manual; N-45 keeps tick 48 h, daily 30 d, monthly 12 months, manual until the owner's cleanup card (backup.retention in config).

true: the decompressed copy was opened read-only, PRAGMA integrity_check returned ok, count(*) of records equals row_count, max(seq) equals high_water_seq, min(seq) is at or above min_retained_seq, and store:epoch in the copy equals epoch.
The off-host path and its checksum when the mirror succeeded, else absent; a failed mirror is backup.mirror_failed 500 and the local backup still counts, but the off-host age keeps growing.

output.record: After 3 attempts: the stage that failed (snapshot, compress, verify, write), the error, the attempts; one card through N-28 because a store with no fresh backup is an owner-acts state.

mechanism.component: Go package scheduler/internal/backup: Run(class), Verify(path), Prune is not here. It calls N-01's Snapshot, which runs VACUUM INTO a temp path under STATE/backup/store/tmp/ on N-01's dedicated reader connection: one read transaction, so the copy is one consistent image while commits continue (nodes/N-01/spec.xml#mechanism). The writer is never held.
zstd level 3 (the Go zstd library pinned in the module; no shelling out), streaming, so a 1 GiB file needs no 1 GiB of memory.

STATE/backup/store/YYYY/MM/ by the UTC day of the snapshot; one file per backup; a README.md at STATE/backup/store/ names the writer, the classes, the retention and the cleanup script (owner, C35: cleanup scripts for every artifact).

backup.mirror_dir: a directory on another host (a share of the owner's NAS or a Pi of the cluster mounted over the tailnet; Windows mounts of the same machine do not count, because they die with it). Copy, read back, checksum compare; never the primary. Which host is an owner decision not yet made (as with shared/outside-probe.xml#availability); until it is set the off-host age is unbounded and its alarm stands as one card. No cloud target is built in: the owner's S3 bucket needs the privileged profile, which is user-initiated only (global hard rule).

The gauge backup.offhost_age_hours is the age of the newest verified backup whose mirror read back equal. Over backup.rpo_offhost_hours it is owner-acts once per transition (one card through N-28), and the restore bound of shared/contracts.xml#restore names it as the data-loss bound for a host loss.
mechanism.mermaid: flowchart LR T[backup tick, class] --> S[N-01 Snapshot on its reader connection: VACUUM INTO tmp] S --> Z[zstd stream to tmp.zst] Z --> V[decompress, integrity_check, count = row_count, max = high_water_seq, min ge min_retained_seq] V -- ok --> R[rename to final path, fsync dir] V -- not ok --> F[attempt + 1, up to 3] R --> C[sha256 both, write README if absent] C --> M{mirror_dir set?} M -- yes --> Y[copy, checksum compare] M -- no --> B Y --> B[append backup 201] F --> B2[backup.failed 500 after 3]
mechanism.step: Acquire the maintenance lease backup:store (allowed under hold, shared/contracts.xml#lease-machine) in a Commit whose precondition is that no live drain:<resource> lease covers the target snapshot path or STATE/backup/store/tmp/ (N-45 drains before it cleans, nodes/N-45/spec.xml#mechanism); a live drain lease refuses the allocation with backup.busy 423 reason drained and the next tick retries. Then ask N-01 for Snapshot(tmp); the reply carries epoch, high_water_seq, row_count, min_retained_seq and bytes.
Compress to tmp.zst; compute sha256 of the raw file while reading it.

Verify: decompress to a second temp file, open read-only, PRAGMA integrity_check must be exactly ok, SELECT count(*) FROM records must equal row_count, SELECT max(seq) must equal high_water_seq, SELECT min(seq) must be at or above min_retained_seq, and store:epoch must equal epoch. Any difference is a failed attempt.
Rename tmp.zst to the final path; fsync the directory; sha256 the compressed file.

Mirror when configured: copy to mirror_dir with the same relative path, read it back, compare sha256; a mismatch deletes the mirror copy and reports backup.mirror_failed 500 (3 attempts); the primary record is still 201.

One Commit with operation key N-05/backup/<class>@<tick_n>/r1: backups.append writes the row and appends backup 201 with everything above; the entity backup:latest is CAS-updated so cleanup-store.sh and the restore have one place to look.
Delete every temp file in STATE/backup/store/tmp/ older than one hour at the start of every run (a crashed run leaves temps; this is their cleanup).
mechanism.restore-drill: On the daily class, after the backup, run Verify on the newest backup of the previous day as well, so a backup that rotted on disk is found within a day and reported as backup.rotten 500.

start.rule: Nothing starts by an agent typing. N-06 emits the backup tick from the service clock; the schedule is config; the first tick after start runs at once when the newest backup is older than backup.interval_seconds (a restart never skips a due backup).
start.step: At start: create STATE/backup/store/ and tmp/ 0700; write README.md if absent; read the backups table for the newest verified row; if none or older than the interval, run a tick-class backup now.
Check free space under STATE against backup.min_free_mib 2048; under it, backup.disk 503 once and the run is skipped until N-45 frees space.
backup.started 100 with the newest backup's age.

wait.name: snapshot
wait.fallback: a failed attempt; the writer is released by context cancel; the store keeps serving

wait.name: compress-verify
wait.fallback: a failed attempt; temps are removed

wait.name: mirror
wait.fallback: backup.mirror_failed 500; the local backup stands; an unmounted mirror is reported once per transition, not per tick

wait.name: disk
wait.fallback: backup.disk 503; N-45 runs cleanup; owner card if still under after cleanup

wait.name: interval
wait.fallback: N-06 reports tick.missed when a tick is late by two intervals; the next tick runs

retries.rule: Every automated step retries up to 3 times, then recovers and reports.
retries.step: Any stage failing restarts the run from the snapshot, 3 attempts with 30, 60, 120 s between; the fourth is backup.failed 500 with the stage and the error; one card through N-28; the next scheduled tick tries again regardless, because a transient disk error should not need the owner to re-arm anything.
3 attempts inside the run; then backup.mirror_failed 500; the primary is not retried for a mirror failure.
A previous day's backup failing Verify is reported once; the next backup is not affected; the owner's card says which file and that newer ones verified.

many-agents.reading: Any node and the owner read the backups table and backup:latest; a seat never needs a backup; the restore runbook (N-01) reads the latest verified row.
many-agents.working: One backup runs at a time: the run holds the maintenance lease backup:store (shared/contracts.xml#lease-machine) and releases it at the end; N-05 writes no flag entity (N-44 is the only flag writer); a backup.now while the lease is live returns backup.busy 423 and is not queued, because the next tick will cover it.
many-agents.collision: A scheduled tick and a backup.now in the same minute: the flag admits one; the other is 423; the one that ran is of the class that won; a manual class is never downgraded, so if the manual one lost, N-50 or N-49 retries after backup.min_interval_seconds and gets its manual copy.

The snapshot is one consistent image while commits continue: VACUUM INTO runs on N-01's reader connection in one read transaction and never takes the writer; high_water_seq names the boundary exactly. Probe evidence at baseline: 9,788 writes committed during a 2.84 s copy, worst write 184 ms (report D, a model of the store; the built proof is not-run).

N-45 deletes old records while a backup runs: the copy is one read transaction, so it holds the rows as of its start; min_retained_seq in the copy is the floor at that moment, and the verifier's min check uses it.
N-45 prunes while a backup writes: the new file is under tmp/ until rename, and N-45 prunes only rows in the backups table with a past retention date, so an in-progress backup is invisible to it.
The service restarts mid-run: the temp files are removed at the next start (step 7 of the mechanism), the backup:store lease is swept by N-02 recover, and the due check runs a backup at once.
many-agents.test: With the fake clock: 10 days of ticks with Puts between them, one backup.now storm of 5 calls, one injected verify failure and one injected disk-full: every record's class is right, exactly one run at a time, the failure retried 3 times and reported once, the disk-full skipped with one 503, and every surviving file verifies.

emits.acts: N-45 (retention, by $ref to $defs/backup), N-01 runbook (restore), cleanup-store.sh (precondition)
the caller of backup.now, which may retry after min_interval
N-41 alert; the owner card comes from the off-host age passing backup.rpo_offhost_hours
owner, one card: a stored backup fails verification
N-45 cleanup, then owner through a card

status-codes.rule: Every code above must exist in ../../shared/status-codes.xml#codes with the same meaning and actor.

path.cleanup: scheduler/host/bin/cleanup-backups.sh: --dry-run lists files whose backups row is past its retention class and files with no row (orphans); --apply deletes them and marks the rows pruned; it never deletes the newest verified backup of any class, whatever its age
removed by the run itself at start; scheduler/host/bin/cleanup-backups.sh --apply removes anything left over an hour old
scheduler/host/bin/cleanup-backups.sh --mirror applies the same retention to the mirror; it refuses when the mirror is not mounted
rows are pruned with their files by cleanup-backups.sh

state-paths.rule: The hand backups under STATE/backup/2026/10/ (L02 S19) are a different tree: N-49 disposes of them; this node never writes there.

re-entry.note: backup.now of class manual before each cleanup or cut-over step

item.proof: Go test with a writer loop during Snapshot (not-run).

item.proof: Golden record in the test; C22 on #examples.

item.check: With no mirror configured, or a mirror failing past backup.rpo_offhost_hours, the off-host gauge alarms once.
item.proof: Go test with the fake clock (not-run).

item.check: A verify failure is retried 3 times then reported once as backup.failed with the stage.
item.proof: Go test with an injected corrupt copy.

A restart mid-run leaves no temp file and runs a due backup at once.
item.proof: Test with a prepared tmp/ and a stale backups row.

item.proof: Go test with a mirror dir on a tmpfs.

actor.name: N-05 in-process
actor.may: Snapshot, write under STATE/backup/store and the mirror, write the backups rows

actor.name: owner
actor.may: `scheduler ctl backup now`, `scheduler ctl backup list`, set backup.mirror_dir, run cleanup-backups.sh; any cloud copy is the owner's own script with the owner's own credential, user-initiated, never this node

gauge.name: backup.newest_verified_high_water_seq
gauge.note: compared with store.high_water_seq in the same epoch gives the records at risk

gauge.name: backup.offhost_age_hours
gauge.alarm: over backup.rpo_offhost_hours: one card per transition

gauge.name: backup.mirror_ok
gauge.note: 1 when the last off-host copy read back equal, 0 otherwise

monitoring.surface: Map screen (N-38) shows the backup machine with a lamp (fresh, due, failed); Stats (N-40) shows age and bytes; Alerts (N-41) shows backup.failed and backup.rotten; the Controls screen (N-42) has the backup-now button, which is an owner control.action through N-29.

runbook.task: `scheduler ctl backup list` prints every row with class, verified, epoch, high_water_seq, row_count, bytes, path, mirror, pruned.
`scheduler ctl backup now` (class manual); 423 means one is running; wait a minute.
`scheduler ctl backup verify PATH` runs the same Verify as the run.
See ../N-01/spec.xml#runbook restore; it takes the path from `backup list`.
Set backup.mirror_dir through a ticket to a directory mounted from another host; `scheduler ctl reload`; the next run mirrors and the off-host gauge resets.

item.what: hand backups of state by the orchestrator and architect (S19: 17 directories, 25 MB, 5,902 files, read by nobody)
item.reason: L02 section 8 item 7: named, dated, reasoned backups of hand fixes should become an automated record kind; a backup is a scheduled record here, and the hand tree is disposed of by N-49

item.what: the backup-home skill: tar of HOME to S3 with the minecraft-admin profile
item.reason: the profile is privileged and user-initiated only (global hard rule); a factory node may never select it; a cloud mirror is the owner's own script

item.what: the suspended jenkins-backup CronJob and the SMB-mounted JENKINS_HOME as the pattern
item.reason: that is Jenkins' home (N-20 Longhorn home); the factory store is on the host and its backup is this node; a CronJob cannot reach the host file
retention lives on each backup record as a class and N-45 prunes by it; one place, data, not two timers
no shelling out from the service; VACUUM INTO on the store's reader connection is transaction-consistent and needs no second binary

item.what: VACUUM INTO under the writer's turn and a verifier comparing count with the top seq (book 1.0)
item.reason: the first blocks every commit for the copy (2.82 s on 293.7 MiB, report D), the second fails as soon as retention deletes a row (F14)

item.what: daily, weekly, monthly classes, STATE/backups/ and a 1024 MiB floor (book 1.0)
item.reason: two vocabularies for one table; tick, daily, monthly, manual under STATE/backup/store/ with the 2048 MiB floor is the one (NF-A10)
